etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English snake, from Old English snaca (“snake, serpent, reptile”), from Proto-West Germanic *snakō (“snake”) (compare German Low German Snake, Snaak (“snake”), dialectal German Schnake (“adder”), Swedish snok (“grass snake”), Icelandic snákur (“snake”)), derived via Proto-Germanic *snakô from Proto-Germanic *snakaną (“to crawl”) (compare Old High German snahhan), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)neg- (“to crawl; a creeping thing”). Cognate with Sanskrit नाग (nāgá, “snake”)). Doublet of nāga.

definitions.definition: A legless reptile of the suborder Serpentes with a long, thin body and a fork-shaped tongue.

quote.citation: 1892, Oscar Wilde, A House of Pomegranates‎[1]:
quote.text: The man writhed like a trampled snake, and a red foam bubbled from his lips.

quote.citation: 1950 April, Timothy H. Cobb, “The Kenya-Uganda Railway”, in Railway Magazine, page 263:
quote.text: After dark the train is a lighted snake, as, even when the passengers' lights are out, each carriage has a side-light in the middle just under the eaves.
Mrs. Kenwigs was horror-stricken to think that she should ever have nourished in her bosom such a snake, adder, viper, serpent, and base crocodile, as Henrietta Petowker.

quote.citation: 2021, Peter McKenna, 5:51 from the start, in Kin, season 1, episode 2, spoken by Frank Kinsella (Aidan Gillen):
quote.text: Well, if it was Moore, he's a fucking snake.

definitions.definition: A person who acts deceitfully for social gain.
A tool to aid cable pulling.
(UK, Australia) A flavoured jube (confectionary) in the shape of a snake.

quote.citation: 2017 April 7, “War Dub”, performed by Little T (Josh Tate):
quote.text: Yo, bare people and the snakes, yeah, they're just grass / Next minute you're the mate, yeah / Next day stab in the back

definitions.definition: (finance, historical) Short for snake in the tunnel.

quote.citation: 2001, W. Bonefeld, The Politics of Europe: Monetary Union and Class, page 69:
quote.text: The snake failed to provide an anchor for currency stability and, through it, disinflation.

definitions.definition: Short for black snake (“firework that creates a trail of ash”).
(intransitive) To follow or move in a winding route.

quote.citation: 1996 September 24, Mark Addinall, “Football fever...”, in aus.personals‎[3] (Usenet):
quote.text: Any Brisbane female interested in snaking down a few beers whilst watching the footy on a big screen?

quote.citation: 2021 December 29, Stephen Roberts, “Stories and facts behind railway plaques: Bournemouth (circa 1880)”, in RAIL, number 947, pages 59–60:
quote.text: Opened in June of that year [1880], the station was the southern terminus of the much-lamented Somerset and Dorset Joint Railway (the S&D  or 'Slow and Dirty'), which snaked its way down from Bath.

quote.citation: 2001 April 5, Hyena, “Home made supercharger ?”, in aus.cars‎[4] (Usenet):
quote.text: Although it wouldn't be the first time some one patented an idea that I'd had a year earlier. […] Someone already has :) […] F*CK ME !!  Snaked again !

definitions.definition: (transitive) To clean using a plumbing snake.
(US, informal) To drag or draw, as a snake from a hole; often with out.

quote.citation: November 27 1835, N.B. St. John, letter to George Thompson
quote.text: his wife and children shall not be forced to flee from the hearth of a friend, lest they should be snaked out by men in civic authority

definitions.definition: (nautical) To wind round spirally, as a large rope with a smaller, or with cord, the small rope lying in the spaces between the strands of the large one; to worm.
